answer: Each AI grader carries a cryptographic pigment token that encodes a unique biometric bloom, similar to a lotus seed, issued by a decentralized reef of validators. Periodically a random jury of validators is drawn to audit a sample of grading decisions; the auditors recompute the pigment hash and verify the bloom matches the original issuance, rejecting any mismatch. An attacker must forge a fresh pigment for every fake identity and pay the full issuance fee for each, making a Sybil burst cost linear in the number of impostors.
